input.quote: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.
input.rationale: Section 24 tracks our preferred position: Customer may assign freely to an Affiliate or an M&A successor on notice (24.1); Vendor needs our consent for assignment, delegation or change of control and may never assign to a Customer competitor (24.2); other assignments require consent not unreasonably withheld (24.3); and Vendor gets no termination, suspension or repricing right on our change of control (24.4). Section 13.3 consistently permits transfer of licence rights with a permitted assignment. No redline needed.

input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.1 correctly leaves Customer Data and our pre-existing IP with us and 14.4 bars joint ownership, but 14.2 reverses our position on paid-for work product: Vendor owns every Deliverable and we get only a revocable, non-transferable term licence, so we lose access to what we paid for on expiry. We flipped ownership to Customer with an assignment (and a perpetual, irrevocable, transferable fallback licence); Vendor still retains Vendor Technology under 14.3 with the Section 13.2 perpetual licence.
